newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Monday following the decline of the U.S. currency against the mark, dealers said.
"Local forex trading continues to be influenced by the movements of the dollar abroad. The shekel rose today following the decline of the dollar against the mark," said Zahi Elias of Bank Leumi.
"The Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market but on a relatively small scale buying more than $70 million," Elias said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for more than a month.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
"The market did not react to expectations that the Bank of Israel would cut its key interest rate. If it does reduce the rate it might have some impact on trading later today," Elias added.
The Bank of Israel was scheduled to announce its key lending rate for March at 1430 GMT today.
Analysts said the central bank would either leave the base rate unchanged or cut it up to 0.3 percentage point from the current 14.2 percent.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3420 shekels against 3.3510 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6407 shekels against 3.6386 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7332 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7115 on Friday and against the mark at 1.9944 shekels against 1.9851 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3405 shekels.
